name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
description: VoiceAssistant-Eval is a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, and spoken dialogue for listening; multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and various scenarios for speaking; and highly heterogeneous images for viewing. The benchmark addresses four key weaknesses in existing benchmarks: lack of voice personalization evaluation, limited focus on hands-free interaction, neglect of various audio contexts in daily life, and insufficient multi-modal (vision+audio) integration assessment.
creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li (CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK)
citeAs: Wang, K., Ren, H., Lu, Z., Zhan, M., & Li, H. (2025). VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing. arXiv:2509.22651.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from 47 source datasets spanning audio understanding, speech, music, sound, and vision domains. For listening tasks, source data was drawn from 23 audio understanding datasets. For speaking tasks, data came from 22 datasets including 11 text datasets and 11 audio datasets. For viewing tasks, MMMU was used as the source dataset. Role-play voice profiles were curated by selecting 100 distinct roles with three representative audio clips per role. Text instructions were converted to audio using three TTS models (F5TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B), with quality filtering using UTMOS Strong (threshold 3.8) and transcription verification using Whisper-Large-v3.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 10% of candidates were removed during the validation stage due to corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and demonstrably incorrect answers.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data was extracted from 47 source datasets including: MMMU, VocalBench, AlpacaEval, MMSU, RoleBench, AdvBench, AIR-Bench, MEAD, BeaverTails-Eval, MT-Bench-101, VCTK, IFEval, MusicCaps, CommonVoice, SD-Eval, Nsynth, BIG-Bench Hard, Clotho, SLURP, VoiceBench, MTJ-Jamendo, JL Corpus, MELD, AudioCaps, AudioGrounding, CoVoST 2, LibriSpeech, VocalSound, VoxCeleb1, MUSIC-AVQA, FoR, SpeechInstructBench, IEMOCAP, FollowBench, SpokenWOZ, TUT2017, AVQA, CommonsenseQA, GSM8K, STORAL, Clotho-AQA, FMA, CochlScene, Fisher, MT Bench, RAVDESS, MyST.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text instructions were preprocessed for TTS synthesis: (1) image references replaced with descriptive phrases; (2) text rewritten using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for TTS suitability (numbers, math expressions converted to spoken form); (3) multiple-choice options rephrased for better readability. Speech was synthesized using F5TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B, with UTMOS Strong quality filtering (threshold 3.8) and Whisper-Large-v3 transcription for WER-based selection. In total, 13,471 high-quality speech audio files were synthesized.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A four-stage curation process was applied: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance, with manual review of suspected duplicates, resulting in 15,359 samples; (2) Validation excluding entries with corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and incorrect answers (approximately 10% discarded); (3) Categorization assigning problems to 13 predefined task categories based on source metadata; (4) Balanced sampling to equalize category representation, resulting in 10,497 final samples.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Content quality was assessed using gpt-oss-20b with thirteen task-specific evaluator prompts covering listening, speaking, and viewing tasks. For emotion tasks, emotion2vec was used to obtain emotion probabilities. Speech quality was measured using UTMOS. Consistency between text and speech was evaluated by transcribing speech outputs with Whisper-Large-v3 and computing modified Word Error Rate (WER). For role-play tasks, Wespeaker was used to calculate speaker similarity between model-generated speech and reference role audio. Human evaluation was conducted on 10% of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B responses (1,050 examples) across all 13 tasks for validation.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom lightweight web-based curation tool was built for manual quality review. Curators reviewed each item on a single screen with inline audio players, image viewers, transcripts, and multiple-choice options, assigning Good or Bad verdicts with optional notes.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation validation showed strong agreement between automated gpt-oss-20b scoring and human judgments, with Pearson correlation coefficients ranging from 0.73 to 1.00 (overall 0.92) and agreement rates uniformly above 90% (overall 96.1%). Evaluation stability was assessed by repeating scoring 10 times on 10% of samples, showing low variance (standard deviations mostly below 3). Statistical significance testing using paired two-sided t-tests with Bonferroni correction confirmed reliability of performance differences.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each item receives scores across three dimensions: content quality (via LLM judge), speech quality (via UTMOS), and consistency (via modified WER). Role-play items additionally receive speaker similarity scores via Wespeaker.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: gpt-oss-20b (content quality evaluation), UTMOS Strong / UTMOS (speech quality evaluation), Whisper-Large-v3 (speech transcription and WER computation), emotion2vec (emotion probability estimation), Wespeaker (speaker similarity for role-play tasks), F5TTS / ChatTTS / Dia-1.6B (speech synthesis), Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (text rewriting for TTS preprocessing)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and evaluation code will be publicly released under an MIT license. The authors bear responsibility in case of violation of rights. A data governance process for auditing and removal is maintained, with the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes role-play voice imitation tasks with speaker audio clips (100 distinct roles, 3 audio clips per role). The dataset includes 7 user emotion categories (angry, disgusted, fearful, happy, neutral, sad, surprised). Five Chinese roles are included in the role-play task.
rai:dataSocialImpact: VoiceAssistant-Eval aims to advance the development of voice-first AI assistants applicable in healthcare, education, smart homes, customer service, and automotive industries. The benchmark identifies gaps in safety alignment and robustness, encouraging development of more trustworthy and reliable voice assistants. The role-play subset raises concerns about voice cloning misuse (identity spoofing, harassment, fraud), addressed through prohibitions on training models to reproduce identifiable speakers without consent, requirements for consent gating and watermarking, and provision of safety cards describing acceptable use and known risks.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is primarily in English, with only five Chinese roles in the role-play task, limiting generalizability to diverse linguistic settings. Questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, which may not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments. The role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles that may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. Evaluation relies on GPT-based scoring, which may favor certain phrasings or overlook nuanced errors.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is monolingual (English, with five Chinese roles), limiting generalization to diverse linguistic settings. The range of evaluated models is limited, with only one proprietary system (GPT-4o-Audio) included. The evaluation relies on automated measures and GPT-based scoring, which may introduce noise and bias. The benchmark evaluates models in an offline, static manner and does not measure latency, real-time processing, barge-in handling, or error recovery. Video-audio integration and continuous audio-visual streaming tasks are not covered. The dataset should not be used for training models for cheating on the benchmark.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for Testing and Evaluation of voice AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. Specific use cases include: evaluating audio understanding (natural sounds, music, speech), assessing voice personalization and speaker imitation, testing hands-free voice interaction, evaluating multi-modal (audio+visual) integration, benchmarking safety alignment and robustness of voice assistants, and tracking progress toward next-generation multimodal AI assistants. The dataset is not intended for training models to cheat on the benchmark.
